name: TPV
limitations: Heat deflection does not apply to it.
identityNote: Thermoplastic vulcanizates, ISO 18064 TPV: a rubber phase cross-linked as it is mixed into a thermoplastic. purefil's sheet: "TPV is a high-quality thermoplastic vulcanizate... With a Shore A hardness of 92"; no document names its rubber or its matrix. A material of its own, as TPS is (R196), made by the owner's instruction that a product be named for what its maker's documents say it is (D106); until then R201 filed it under TPE, polymer not stated. No polymers.csv row, so the estimate model cannot place it and it is not estimated.

notApplicable.hdt045: HDT is a rigid-bar test. ISO 75 ends at 0.2 % outer-fibre strain, which a bar reaches once its modulus falls to about 225 MPa, so an elastomer has no meaningful HDT and makers list it as N/A. A value an elastomer's sheet publishes is shown and never decides. Sintering filaments are left out too: the finished part is the sintered metal or ceramic.
